origins.section: A Lock per Bin Keeps Every Move Right and Every Total Wrong
A compareAndSet Loop That Reads the Value Once Spins Forever; incrementAndGet Leaves No Loop to Get Wrong
A Double-Checked Flag Can Say Loaded Before the Value Is; a synchronized Getter Can't
One Lock Makes the Total Right; One Owner Thread Also Keeps Readers From Waiting

recorded.rule: Q2 v2: a giveaway, read from the question's own text alone
recorded.prompt:q-report-over-account-locks: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. recorded.because:q-report-over-account-locks: Options form two balanced pairs (a/b 'exact total every night', c/d 'sometimes off'), all similar in length and built the same way ('X, since Y'). No option stands out as longer, more hedged or grammatically different, so the wording does not point to one answer.
